pairs.locus: Aquinas, Summa Theologiae I, q.57 a.4 sed contra (Jer. 17,9-10)
pairs.question: Pravum est cor hominis et inscrutabile, quis cognoscet illud?
pairs.derivation: Scriptural quotation (Ier. 17,9-10) embedded in the sed contra. The question is the genuine interrogative 'quis cognoscet illud?'; the preceding clause 'Pravum est cor hominis et inscrutabile' is kept as verbatim setup so that 'illud' has a referent. The answer is God's reply 'Ego, Dominus, scrutans corda.' The narrative frame 'secundum illud Ier. 17,9-10:' before it is dropped as scaffolding; the verb of speaking is implicit. Nothing between question and answer is omitted.

pairs.locus: Aquinas, Summa Theologiae I, q.57 a.5 sed contra (Isaiah 63,1)
pairs.question: Quis est iste qui venit de Edom?
pairs.derivation: Direct-speech exchange (Isaiae 63,1) embedded in the sed contra: angels ask, Jesus answers. The speech tags 'ubi quaerentibus angelis,' (framing the asking) and 'respondit Iesus:' (framing the reply) are dropped as narration of the exchange. Question and answer are quoted verbatim and contiguous; nothing internal is elided.
